summary: Interpreted the third execution of the fixed extended-window experiment (CheckRun 9d7660152346447a85280b9298e199a1, exit 0). It reproduces the entire settled pattern: nil at 0ms after the partition, nil again at 5398ms while a competing node already led and the answering leader was still Leader inside its 20s lease, that competitor's write at index 5 absent from the old leader's FSM (still Leader, applied 3), and the control losing leadership at 20002ms; all four comparisons hold, and all three executions of this fixed experiment are now cited with joint_history. The same execution also reported near_node_self_voter true again, making that field three for three in this harness against zero for seven runs of the harness that samples the same view together with each node's own log index; I narrowed the open gap with that comparison and recorded why the pre-demotion state cannot explain it (the bootstrapped leader needs ten to twenty seconds to campaign, so followers were caught up in both harnesses), leaving the sampling arrangement as the one named difference and the gap open and owned. The settled claim and its bound are unchanged, since quorumSize and verifyLeader both read the leader's own configuration, which is unambiguous and corroborated by both far nodes; the counterevidence and limits were updated rather than dropped, and no further experiment was submitted with the allocation that remains.
